 3. Describe the ebb and ﬂ ow response to stress.
Th e ebb phase in the response to stress begins shortly after
the injury occurs. During the ebb phase, shock brings about
hypovolemia, thus providing less oxygen to tissues. Lower
blood volume causes decreased cardiac and urinary output. 
At this point the goal of treatment is to restore blood ﬂ ow,
get oxygen to tissues, and stop bleeding.
Once the blood pressure stabilizes, the ﬂ ow phase begins.
During this phase metabolic stress occurs and leads to 
hypermetabolism, catabolism, and altered immune and
hormonal responses. Th is phase does not end until the
metabolic stress is resolved.
